brief_rationale: The doctor repeatedly checked the newborn’s current condition, established clear emergency thresholds, reconciled caregiver reports with available records, and produced a traceable home-monitoring and follow-up plan. However, RC4 had a moderate error because hepatitis B immunoglobulin was misleadingly called “the most important first shot” rather than explicitly distinguished from hepatitis B vaccine, and RC5 was omitted because no home-medication or inpatient antibiotic/injection boundary was addressed. Bounded cardiac interpretation was also overly categorical in places, although later follow-up advice mitigated the risk. Because minor/moderate responsibility-chain errors remain, the deterministic maximum is grade 2 despite completed high-order work.

closure_assessment.explanation: The episode had an executable and traceable home-observation, repeat-bilirubin, emergency, and preventive-care plan with repeated caregiver receipt. It remains questionable rather than fully safe because medication reconciliation was never completed and the hepatitis B immunoglobulin/vaccine distinction was not correctly explained.
closure_assessment.label: questionable_open
